name: hashmap-str
algorithm: String-key hash map churn with each language's standard map and its default string hash: n generated 8-24 byte ASCII keys sliced from one buffer inserted into a map that grows from empty, each looked up once with a hit and once with a miss, every other key removed, all n looked up again; rounds times with a fresh map (README.md).

skip.c: no std hash map in C
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; there is no checked arithmetic to remove

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own map; the checksum (every value found, every miss, every key left) checks that every map held the same keys
notes: Hashes and DoS posture (B20): mk Map.New, DD-5's fast fixed hash, public key; mk-keyed Map.NewKeyed, SipHash-1-3 under a random per-process key; Rust HashMap, SipHash-1-3 under RandomState's random key; Zig StringHashMap, Wyhash with seed 0, fixed; Go map, AES-based runtime hash seeded per map; C# Dictionary<string, ulong>, Marvin32 randomized per process.

All 2n string keys (n present, n guaranteed-absent misses, each 8-24 ASCII bytes) are generated once before the timed rounds from SplitMix64 into one buffer; Mk, Rust, Zig and Go borrow slices of that buffer, and C# constructs its UTF-16 string[] once before the rounds loop.
